label: D2: reached S2 while the agent still leans toward a1 (mostly a1 -> S2 rare)
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the reached state is S2 (never at D1/GO, never on S1, never with a reward input). Within S2 D2 steps (rate 17%), it is selective for the agent leaning toward a1: 90% of activation mass is on a1 -> S2 rare transitions, and the rest on a2 -> S2 common when S1 is the good state. The model own policy logit at that step, choice = logit(a1) - logit(a2) > 1, separates it best (dev P 0.75, R 0.83, F1 0.79, mass recall 0.92). The structural alternative (D2 & state == 2 & action == 1, i.e. rare transition after a1) gets F1 0.72 and mass 0.90. All variables are observed at D2 (the transition is visible then, and choice is the model own readout), so no future variables are used. Higher activations are covered better by the predicate (quartile coverage rises with activation), but I did not check a finer magnitude relationship. Partial because about 25% of predicted steps are inactive and some weak activations fall outside it. It is stronger on the core trial, which is overrepresented in rare/unrewarded patterns, and gets weaker late in the episode (trials 90-99).
